method: Direct inspection of six timestamp-matched reference/output samples and all 77 frames of both generated arms as thumbnails; not a native-resolution video-quality assessment
observations: The reference advances modestly toward the playground; the commanded arm drifts far past it.
Measured frames 13 onward show localized ghosting/duplicated stair and pole edges near the first corrected boundary.
Later measured frames retain a recognizable playground but have altered roof shape and stair/rail appearance relative to reference. The commanded arm also changes structure while drifting.
All-frame thumbnails do not show the sustained near-total loss of recognizable content seen on 02267acf seed 107.
Mean position and rotation errors improve, but the boundary artifact and structural changes prevent a clean visual-control success claim.
classification: Pose benefit with boundary ghosting and altered structure; visual fidelity tradeoff retained, not clean success.
temporal_limitation: All frames are inspected as small static thumbnails; this does not identify physical camera reversal, quantify perceived video quality, or exclude finer artifacts.
